Klarna might reschedule its IPO for September
Klarna might look to IPO as early as September, sources told
Bloomberg. The news comes as fintech stock prices surge
and the U.S. IPO market strengthens. 
Klarna filed for IPO back in March but paused such plans only
a month later after President Trump’s tariff announcements
rattled the market. At the time, Klarna was looking to raise at
least $1 billion and nab a $15 billion valuation. By June,
however, Klarna’s co-founder and CEO, Sebastian
Siemiatkowski, took a different turn. When asked about the
company’s IPO plans, Siemiatkowski only smiled and said he
was “happy there’s less turbulence in the market.” 
Details are slim, though, regarding when Klarna will schedule
its debut; no final decisions have been made, Bloomberg
reported. The company is profitable and was last privately
valued at around $14 billion.
